# Sentences no command may fire inside, in any mode (phase M4). Synthetic.
# Checked in "clause", the most permissive mode, which covers the others.
# Each is ordinary speech, said to an agent or near the microphone, that
# holds a command's words: what the never-fires rules are for.

# An object after the verb.
Stop listening to that song.
Keep listening to me explain.
I keep listening to this podcast, it's great.
Can you stop listening to the radio for me?
Keep listening for the doorbell.
Stay listening to the meeting and summarise it.
Open the mic settings, please.
Turn the mic off on my laptop, it's too loud.
# A negation.
Don't keep listening.
Don't start a new chat, just carry on.
Please don't stop listening to me.
I don't want you to keep listening.
Never stop listening, that's the trick.
Do not open the mic.
# Reported or quoted speech.
He said, keep listening.
She told me: stop listening.
What does "keep listening" do?
The button says "open mic".
I heard him say goodbye.
Tell him I said, goodbye.
My mom always says, keep listening.
The word is: goodbye.
Type 'stop listening' into the box.
# A question about it, not a request.
Keep listening? Why would I?
Should I keep listening?
Why did you stop listening?
Did you keep listening the whole time?
# Two commands, or one said twice.
New chat, and keep listening.
Keep listening. Stop.
Stop listening, keep listening.
Keep listening. Keep listening.
Keep listening, goodbye.

Did you see the new chat feature?

Listen to me carefully, this matters.
Start listening to audiobooks, they say.
Bye the way, hm.
Goodbye, see you tomorrow.
Stop the music, and keep the lights on.
Full stop at the end of the line, please.
Move this to the trash.
# A command's words inside a chat's topic: still two commands' words.
Continue the chat about how to keep listening. What did we decide?
